best_for: Threema users who want to type replies on a computer and keep their phone nearby and online while they do.

points.title: This is the older desktop app
points.text: Version 1.2.50 is Threema for Desktop 1.x, built on Threema Web inside Electron. Threema now lists it under legacy apps, and the project says it is in maintenance mode.

points.title: Your phone must stay online
points.text: With this version, the Threema app on your phone has to be switched on and connected for every session. If the phone dies, the desktop stops getting messages.

points.title: Desktop 2.0 works without the phone
points.text: Threema's newer Desktop 2.0, in beta at review time, keeps working when the phone is off once linked. One phone can link up to two computers. It is a separate download from Threema, not this listing.

points.title: Paid once, not by subscription
points.text: Threema for private use is a one-time purchase of about 6.00 USD or EUR, depending on app store and country. Threema Work costs 3.00 or 5.00 per user per month, billed yearly. Prices were read on the date below.

points.title: No phone number needed
points.text: You can use Threema without a phone number or SIM card. The desktop client is open source under AGPL-3.0.

points.title: 64-bit systems
points.text: Threema's requirements list Windows 10 21H2 or later and macOS 12 or later, 64-bit. Windows installs per user; the Mac build is universal. This site keeps only the current release for each.
